study.question: Does explicitly exposing chronological alternation between target-matching and nonmatching timestamp groups improve prediction beyond the same groups’ exchangeable composition and the complete count/recency/ordinal incumbent?
study.hypothesis: The latest breadth and provenance implementations failed to improve the incumbent. Source inspection shows its added deterministic summaries encode counts, decay, extrema and anchor ranks, but not adjacency of target match states. The attention includes coarse ages and can indirectly approximate order, so this is an inductive-bias limitation, not a proof of missing information. Histories can have the same number of timestamp groups and same multiset of target-match fractions but different adjacent switches. If this arrangement matters for CTR, providing observed switch rate alongside its exact exchangeable expectation should outperform duplicated expectation at equal capacity. This is a new local hypothesis with no predictive evidence and no verified priority claim.

nearest_work.difference: Inherit the adapted attention/MLP, not an exact DIN reproduction. DIN already discusses local interest activation, unnormalized intensity and unsuccessful generic LSTM sequence modeling. Add deterministic field/action-specific chronological match switching with an exchangeable replacement. This is not a claim to invent sequential interest modeling or run statistics.

README confirms category/brand/action without item IDs and references DIEN; detailed DMR/DIEN mechanisms have not been inspected or reproduced. Only supplied coarse fields used. Authorized sequence/evolution searches found no additional paper; nearest-work coverage is incomplete, novelty unverified.

nearest_work.difference: Preserve r0023 exactly; abandon the unsuccessful cardinality extension. Add observed timestamp-group adjacency, not more set breadth, volume, signed field provenance or crossed-anchor ranks.

inherited_components: entire r0023 parent embedding, attention, static context, count, decay, match/nonmatch extrema, crossed same-action/pooled-fallback ranks and strict-newer complementary volume
fixed supplied histories and causal age boundary; no event acquisition
all existing initialization draws and standard host training objective
study.proposed_difference: For each category/brand and action, sort valid positive-ID events by age and aggregate equal timestamps. Let p_i be target-match fraction of timestamp group i, G its number of groups, S=sum p_i, Q=sum p_i^2. Observed switch rate O=sum_adjacent[p_i+p_j-2p_i*p_j]/(G-1). Exact expectation under uniform permutation of these groups is E=[2*S-2*(S^2+S-Q)/G]/(G-1). Set O=E=0 for G<2 or missing target. Sorting direction is immaterial; no within-timestamp order is inferred. Append16 half-scaled inputs: candidate[E,O], composition control[E,E], capacity/readout control[V,V] where V is inherited newer_count. Every variant computes O,E,V and preserves all parent inputs. No extra RNG calls, optimizer or loss changes.
predictions: Primary predeclared contrast: ordered_switch AUC exceeds exchangeable_switch, and is competitive with the incumbent; Logloss and measured cost must be reported separately. A seed42 result is preliminary only.

O and E differ on some supplied histories; all added inputs remain finite in[0,0.5], zero for empty/missing-target field coordinates, invariant to event-array permutations, positive-ID relabeling and simultaneous-event reorderings.
Exchangeable expectation agrees with exhaustive group permutations in small synthetic cases, including mixed timestamp groups; primary difference must disappear for G<=2 and constant p.
If expectation alone helps, exchangeable_switch can exceed duplicate_volume without supporting chronological alternation.
falsifiers: ordered_switch fails to exceed exchangeable_switch under matched training, or any gain fails paired-seed replication; this is evidence against this implementation, not all sequential models.
O equals E almost everywhere or supported residuals are negligible, making the hypothesized limitation inconsequential.
Any ordering/tie/missing-field invariance, expectation identity, input bound, parent-prefix identity or finite-logit check fails.
A ranking gain accompanied by materially worse Logloss/cost does not establish broad quality or efficiency improvement.
alternative_explanations: Coarse age embeddings and attention already encode the useful arrangement; adjacency adds noise.
Group weighting changes event weighting; effects may reflect timestamp multiplicity rather than temporal switches. E conditions on the exact group-probability multiset, not a model of real behavior.
Duplication, feature scaling and optimization conditioning can change learned trajectories despite matched parameter counts and initial predictions.
Truncation at128, static snapshot as-of uncertainty, coarse IDs, rare-action sparsity, validation reuse and seed noise limit interpretation.
Candidate diagnostics cover first512 impressions only, are self-reported and are not full-population frequencies or causal effects.
